heard: This colossal cluster pumps out hundreds of stars every year. Its central black hole weighs roughly 10 billion suns. Normally, that beast should act like a cosmic heater. It should blast radiation that stops gas from forming new stars. Instead, astronomers only detected extreme hot and cold gas. For over a decade, a massive missing link baffled scientists. NASA's Webb Space Telescope mapped a hidden halo of intermediate gas. This warm gas glows like a neon sign, feeding that colossal cluster.
